blocks.value: In the Movement phase, you will be able to move each of your units across the battlefield. Reinforcements can also arrive in this phase to bolster your forces.
The Movement phase is resolved by following these steps:

requirements.obligation: Move each active unit through start/body/end; arrivals are Movement work

blocks.value: Rules that are triggered at the start of the Movement phase are resolved now.

requirements.obligation: Resolve nonempty start-of-phase rule before unit selection

blocks.value: The active player moves their units one at a time, using the sequence below, until all of their units have been selected to move and those moves have ended.

1. Select Unit: Select one friendly unit that has not been selected to move this phase. You can select a unit on the battlefield, in strategic reserves, or embarked within a TRANSPORT. That unit is selected to move.
2. Select Move Type: Select one move type that unit is eligible to make, and resolve it with that unit. This can be one listed below, or one presented elsewhere:

requirements.obligation: Active player chooses a fresh friendly unit, one at a time, including off-board locations

assertions: assert 'remain_stationary' in {o.option_id for o in request.options}
assert unit.unit_instance_id not in {o.option_id for o in following.options}
assert all(('enemy:' not in o.option_id for o in following.options))
assert not [e for e in events(session, 'rule_trigger_observed') if e.get('trigger_kind') == 'move_completion']

assert 'disembark' in {o.option_id for o in request.options}

blocks.value: When the Move Units step ends, the active player must have selected all of their units to make a move with, including those in strategic reserves. This means that before the phase ends, every unit in their army will have been selected to make a move, even if it is to remain stationary (09.04). Any units the active player does not select a move type for during this step will remain stationary.

requirements.obligation: Every unit must be selected and finish, including stationary reserves

assertions: assert 'remain_stationary' in {o.option_id for o in request.options}

blocks.value: Some rules instruct you to select a mode, such as fall-back moves (09.07). Modes are mutually exclusive, and you must assess each one in the order presented. When making a move, if your unit does not meet the conditions of any of the modes, it cannot make that move.

Sometimes a mode will be mandatory if applicable (e.g. consolidation modes, 12.08), but in the case of fall-back moves, ordered retreat is not mandatory, so you could select desperate escape instead.
Many move types state conditions you must meet while/after moving. Those that are labelled with a mode name only apply if you selected that mode; those not labelled with a mode name always apply.

requirements.obligation: Modes are exclusive, unmet modes unavailable; Ordered Retreat is optional
Mode-specific transit permission and common unengaged endpoint

blocks.value: • Ordered Retreat: If your unit is not battle-shocked, you can select this mode.
• Desperate Escape: Otherwise, you must select this mode. Make a hazard roll for each model in your unit (06.03).
• Desperate Escape: Each model that is moved can be moved through enemy models.
Your unit moves as described in Moving (03).
• Until the end of the turn, unless otherwise stated, your unit is not eligible to shoot, declare a charge or start an action.
• Desperate Escape: If your unit is not battle-shocked, you must make a battle-shock roll for your unit (01.07).

blocks.value: Some rules may reference the term 'Desperate Escape test'. In all instances this means the hazard rolls made for the desperate escape mode of a fall-back move.
Abilities that subtract from a unit's Desperate Escape test instead subtract from those hazard rolls.

Example: A battle-shocked unit makes a fall-back move away from a unit of Bloodletters that have the Bane of Cowards ability. As a result of Bane of Cowards, because the unit making the fall-back move is battle-shocked, the hazard rolls they make as part of their desperate escape will be at -1 .

requirements.obligation: Desperate Escape test means hazards (not model removals)

assertions: assert failed > 0, 'This retained seed must exercise a failed hazard.'
assert sum((m.current_wounds for m in current.alive_models())) == sum((m.initial_wounds for m in unit.own_models)) - failed

requirements.obligation: Desperate Escape penalty modifies hazard; real Bane of Cowards example
